loop: Drone launcher designer-led study through pursuit, return and drift; shared flight instrument changes and clean-session handoff, 2026-11-25. Assessment uses the coordinating session context supplied to the closeout worker.
worked: Incremental designer feedback kept accepted fitting, launch and propulsion choices distinct from unsettled behavior and production adoption.
Reusing actual Fighter engine and stabilizer responses, with cached pilot responses and the production impulse taper, provided a coherent basis for the live flight exploration.
Two courses demonstrated real range-triggered Pursuit-to-Return and Pursuit-to-Drift transitions while keeping the inspection bounded to one drone.
Independent browser review complemented study tests, type checks and lint by checking launch eligibility, controls, seeking and visible motion.
Static captures preserved accepted exploration while removing obsolete live apparatus, and the continuation brief records provisional questions and verification limits for the next session.

issues.observation: The initial plume was faint despite automated checks and review; the designer corrected its readability.
issues.effect: Visual tuning had to continue after checks had passed.
issues.interpretation: The checks performed did not establish the desired visual readability; the context does not establish a broader testing defect.

issues.observation: The original fabricated angular-rate response did not feel stabilized to the designer.
issues.effect: The study changed to actual Fighter engine and stabilizer responses, including counterburn.
issues.interpretation: The simplified response was insufficient for this exploration; this does not establish that every study needs production physics.

issues.observation: Repeated fixture tuning attempted to show all three flight modes within one 14-second course; a launch-gate requirement changed that setup assumption.
issues.effect: Additional scene tuning was needed before settling on two courses with actual threshold transitions.
issues.interpretation: Trying to combine the cases appears to have increased iteration effort; the supplied context does not quantify that cost.

issues.observation: Raw less-than distance text in MDX caused a rendering error after type checks passed.
issues.effect: The text was rewritten in words and the browser surface was checked again.
issues.interpretation: Type checks in this loop did not catch this MDX rendering failure; its wider coverage implications were not investigated.

issues.observation: A stale Vite dynamic import followed apparatus deletions.
issues.effect: The shared preview needed one restart before verification could continue.

issues.observation: One CUA tab was already held by another session, and HMR resets interfered with visual checking during edits.
issues.effect: Verification used a fresh capture tab and required edit coordination to keep scenes stable.
issues.interpretation: Concurrent editing and browser use appear to have contributed to coordination overhead; the precise causes were not investigated during closeout.

issues.observation: At the 1× overview the drone was very small and the decorative world gradient could not be independently resolved; the optional fidelity measurement was updated but not rerun.
issues.effect: The handoff limits its visual and measurement claims and records how to locate the drone by plume and range circle.
